# Duration

A span of time: seconds and a fraction, normalized.

```rux
pub struct Duration {
    pub seconds: int64;
    // private fields
}
```

`Copy`. The value is `seconds + nanoseconds / 1e9`, and `nanoseconds` is always in [0, 1e9).

## Fields

| Name      | Type    | Description                           |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `seconds` | `int64` | The whole seconds, carrying the sign. |

## Implements Display

`Duration` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    self: &Duration,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the span as signed decimal seconds followed by `s`.
The magnitude is recomputed from the normalized representation rather than read off it: a negative duration
stores minus one and a half seconds as seconds = -2 with a fraction of 0.5, so printing the fields as they
sit would say "-2.5s".
A precision names exactly that many fractional digits, 0 through 9, and truncates. Without one the fraction
is written to the digits it has with trailing zeros trimmed, and omitted when it is zero, so a whole number
of seconds renders as one.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for a style other than `seconds` or for a
precision past nine.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole rendering was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Duration.rux#L108)

<h3 id="parse-duration"><code>ParseDuration</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ParseDuration(text: char8[..]) -> Duration ! TimeParseError
```

Reads a span written as signed decimal seconds followed by `s`.
Accepts what `Display` writes: an optional sign, at least one digit, an optional fraction of up to nine digits,
and a closing `s`. A leading `+` is accepted and means the same as no sign.
Reports `InvalidSyntax` with the byte offset where the shape stopped matching, and `ExcessiveFraction` at the
first digit that a nanosecond cannot hold. A magnitude too large for the representation is `InvalidSyntax` at
the digit that overflowed, since the text is well formed and the value simply is not one.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/DurationText.rux#L141)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type        | Description      |
| ------ | ----------- | ---------------- |
| `text` | `char8[..]` | the text to read |

**Returns**: the span, or why the text is not one
